title: Python SDK: async-iterator streaming + backpressure-friendly event API
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Background: Our Python SDK currently offers streaming chat primitives that were originally designed around callback handlers and low-level event dispatch. Feedback from SDK users and internal infra teams shows this shape is awkward for modern async code: callbacks complicate cancellation, make resource cleanup error-prone, and don't compose well with async for/async with patterns. Goal: introduce an ergonomic async-iterator (async generator) event API for streaming chat completions that supports backpressure, explicit cancellation, structured event types, and built-in retry semantics for transient transport errors. This ticket scopes design + implementation + tests + migration docs for the core API surface and one canonical example.
proposal: Provide two first-class streaming entrypoints in the Python SDK: 1) Chat.stream_messages(...) -> AsyncIterator[ChatMessageEvent] which yields typed events (token, delta, metadata, done, error) and supports awaitable backpressure via natural async iteration. 2) Chat.stream_responses(..., as_strings=True) -> AsyncIterator[str] for a simpler token/partial text generator. Implement automatic resumable retry for idempotent retries (network timeouts, transient HTTP 5xx) by capturing stream cursor (KV cursor / last_token_id) where the model/transport supports it, with an opt-in parameter retry_policy. Ensure integration with existing sync callbacks via a small adapter utility and provide an 'iter_timeout' parameter to bound time between events. Expose a ContextManager that ensures proper cleanup when consumers abandon iteration (for cancellation and draining).
api_sketch:
# Example API shapes to ship in 0.24.0

# Typed event model (pseudocode)
# ChatMessageEvent: type: 'token'|'delta'|'meta'|'done'|'error', text: Optional[str], token_id: Optional[str], seq: int, meta: dict

# Streaming iterator usage
async for ev in client.chat.stream_messages(model="redwood-compact-1", prompt=prompt):
    if ev.type == 'token':
        # backpressure: if consumer does heavy work, iteration naturally slows the server fetches
        buffer.append(ev.text)
    elif ev.type == 'meta':
        logger.debug('model step', ev.meta)
    elif ev.type == 'error':
        # error event may include transient/terminal classification
        raise StreamError(ev.text)

# Simple generator for text
def assemble():
    async for chunk in client.chat.stream_responses(...):
        output += chunk

# Cancellation via context manager to ensure connection closes
async with client.chat.stream_context(model="redwood-compact-1", prompt=prompt) as stream:
    async for ev in stream:
        if stop_condition(ev):
            break
    # exiting async with ensures we drain/close underlying socket
acceptance_criteria: API delivers an async iterator `stream_messages` that yields typed events and a simpler `stream_responses` text iterator

Backpressure is honored: slow consumers do not cause unbounded memory growth or drop tokens; integration tests simulate slow consumer and confirm memory remains bounded (<50MB growth after 10k tokens)
Cancellation semantics are documented and enforced: using `break` or abandoning iteration triggers graceful connection teardown; `async with stream_context` guarantees cleanup on exception

Automatic transient-retry works with a configurable `retry_policy` and resumes from the last successfully acknowledged token when transport/model supports it; tests stub resumable behavior and validate no duplicated tokens beyond allowed 'at-most-once' semantics for default policy
Migration guide from callback-based streaming exists in docs with copy-paste examples and a small adapter utility `callbacks_to_async_iter`
Unit and integration tests cover: happy path, network timeout → retry+resume, permanent server error → error event, consumer-cancel during mid-stream, and telemetry/tracing context propagation
Type hints and mypy tests included; example type stubs are added to sdk typings package

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Resuming streams is model/transport dependent. Mitigation: default to conservative 'no-resume' for unknown backends; implement resume only for known endpoints and gate behind `supports_resumable_streams` capability flag.

Risk: Consumer misuse leading to leaks if they never iterate through generator. Mitigation: provide context manager and implement __del__ fallback that logs and attempts to close; add lint-warning in docs.

Risk: Retries causing duplicated output if resume semantics are imperfect. Mitigation: make default retry_policy conservative (at-most-once when resume not available), and expose `de_duplication_window` parameter for advanced users.
Risk: Breaking changes for users of callbacks. Mitigation: provide adapter and transitional docs; keep old callback API for one release cycle with deprecation warnings.
qa_plan: Automated unit tests + tox env matrix (py3.9-3.12). Integration: run test server harness that can inject delays, drop connections, and serve resume cursors. Perf smoke: generate 100k tokens across 3 streams with a slow consumer to measure memory and CPU. Add a small manual QA checklist for SDK engineers to verify interactive notebook example and Playground snippet.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: prefer async iterator ergonomics over pushing a heavy callback API — consistent with modern Python async patterns.
Decision: include a thin `stream_context` to make cancellation explicit and reliable.
Decision: default resume/retry is opt-in; safe defaults avoid duplicating tokens.
Trade-off: more complex transport code to support resume cursor capture vs. user-facing ergonomics. We accept complexity in transport to keep SDK API simple.
